sections.h2: Where does a Grayson County, KY deed get recorded?
sections.html:
The Grayson County Clerk records it, at 125 East Market Street in Leitchfield. Under KRS 382.110 a deed has to be filed in the clerk's office of the county where the land lies, or where most of it lies, to bind later purchasers and creditors who had no notice of it.

The Clerk's website lists two numbers for real estate work. Recording and delinquent taxes answer at (270) 259-5295, while licensing, transfers and voter registration use (270) 259-3201. The office reports weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:00 and a Saturday window from 8:00 to 11:00 on the second Saturday of each month, so confirm by phone before a closing that depends on it.

Leitchfield is the county seat and the largest of Grayson County's three cities, which also include Caneyville and Clarkson. A deed for land near either lake, in Big Clifty or in the hills around Millwood is still filed in that one office.

sections.h2: How is the Kentucky transfer tax figured on a Grayson County sale?
sections.html:
The tax is fifty cents for each $500 of value, rounded up for any fraction, and it falls on the grantor named in the deed. The Clerk computes it when the deed is offered for recording and will not accept the deed until the tax is paid. The value is the full consideration, including any liens, or the open-market price if the deed is a gift or states only nominal consideration.

The tax is collected once per transaction. The Clerk retains 5 percent as a collection fee and sends the rest to the county treasurer, who deposits it in the county general fund.

sections.h2: Which Grayson County transfers escape the transfer tax?
sections.html:
KRS 142.050 lists many exemptions. The ones most likely to matter to a house seller are these.

  • A transfer made only to give or release security for a debt.
  • A deed that confirms or corrects one already recorded.
  • Transfers between spouses, or between former spouses as part of a divorce.
  • Transfers under a foreclosure, or a voluntary surrender to the mortgage holder instead of foreclosure.
  • A sale for delinquent taxes or assessments, and a partition.
  • Transfers between parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, for nominal consideration only.

Moves into a trust are also excused where the grantor is the only beneficiary. A Clerk who knowingly records a taxable deed without collecting faces a $50 fine for each offense, which is why the office checks the value stated in the deed.

sections.h2: What does a deed have to say about where the owner got title?
sections.html:
A Kentucky deed must name the immediate source of the grantor's title. When the grantor took title by recorded deed, the new deed cites the earlier one by office, book, page and date of recording. When the land came by inheritance or any route without a recorded writing, the deed states clearly how and from whom the title was obtained.

If the grantor's title came from two or more sources, the deed names each and shows which part of the land came from which. The Clerk may not admit a deed that skips this, though the rule does not apply to deeds made by a court commissioner, sheriff or other court officer acting in that role.

For a Grayson County sale, the practical step is to pull the last vesting deed before drafting the new one. A wrong book and page cite sends the deed back to the preparer.

sections.h2: What deadlines apply to deeds in lieu of foreclosure and commissioner deeds?
sections.html:
A mortgage holder that accepts a deed in lieu of foreclosure must file it with the Clerk no later than 45 days after the deed is executed. For a deed issued by a court-appointed commissioner after a judicial sale, the buyer has five business days after receipt to file it. If 30 business days pass and a city has not seen the filing, the city may ask Circuit Court to compel it and to award costs and attorney fees.

Those deadlines matter to a Grayson County owner in default. Until a deed in lieu is recorded, the public record still shows the borrower as owner.

sections.h2: What happens to delinquent real estate tax in Grayson County?
sections.html:
Kentucky sheriffs hand unpaid bills to the County Clerk after the close of business on April 15, and the Clerk's recording and delinquent tax line is (270) 259-5295. A lien is recorded, and from then on the bill carries 1 percent interest for each month or part of a month, plus commissions for the Clerk and the county attorney.

A sale of the certificates can be scheduled 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and a third-party buyer may add charges. The Department of Revenue's sample bill of $1,000 reaches $1,254 at transfer. Anyone selling a Grayson County house should ask the Clerk for a payoff before the closing date.

sections.h2: What is Grayson County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Grayson County was formed in 1810 from parts of Hardin and Ohio counties and covers 497 square miles of land. Rough River Lake on the northern border and Nolin River Lake to the southeast shape its leisure economy, and some businesses use the label Twin Lakes. Courthouses burned in 1864, 1896 and 1936. The Western Kentucky Parkway, US 62 and the Paducah & Louisville Railroad cross the county, and the Grayson County Airport is also located here.

  • Population: 27,406 in 2025, up 3.7 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Housing units: 13,496, with an owner-occupied rate of 74.6 percent.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $164,600, and median gross rent of $658.
  • Median household income: $50,757, with 22.4 percent of people in poverty.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 36.

With only 36 permits issued, most listings are older houses. A cash sale that closes as-is lets the owner skip repairs and leave tax and recording questions to the title work.

faqs.q: Where is the Grayson County Clerk's office?
faqs.a: At 125 East Market Street in Leitchfield, KY 42754. Recording and delinquent tax questions go to (270) 259-5295, and weekday hours are listed as 8:00 to 4:00.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate transfer tax in Grayson County?
faqs.a: The seller, named as grantor in the deed. The rate is fifty cents per $500 of value, so a $164,600 sale carries $165 of tax, and the Clerk collects it before recording.

faqs.q: Is a deed in lieu of foreclosure charged the transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. KRS 142.050 exempts a voluntary surrender to the mortgage holder in place of foreclosure. The holder must still file the deed with the Clerk within 45 days of signing it.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed leaves out where I got title?
faqs.a: The Clerk cannot admit it to record. A Kentucky deed must cite the prior recorded deed by book and page, or state how the title came by inheritance or other unrecorded means.

faqs.q: Do I owe back property tax before a Grayson County deed is recorded?
faqs.a: The lien stays with the parcel after a sale, so the balance is normally paid at closing. Ask the Clerk's delinquent tax line for a payoff figure first.
